title: Joint custody arrangements - are Indian courts finally adopting them
p1:
A child’s home after divorce may no longer have to mean choosing one parent over the other.

For years, many assumed Indian courts always followed a “one parent wins custody, the other gets visits” approach. But a quiet shift has been taking place.
p2:
The surprising part? Joint custody is not automatically about splitting a child’s time equally between parents. It is about both parents continuing to share responsibility for decisions, care, and the child’s overall well-being.

Indian courts have increasingly recognized that a child benefits from meaningful involvement of both parents, though there is still no separate law that fully defines joint custody.
p3:
Courts today often focus less on parental rights and more on the child’s best interests. Factors like the child’s age, emotional needs, safety, and each parent’s ability to provide care can influence decisions.

The takeaway: joint custody is becoming more accepted, but it is still decided case-by-case rather than being an automatic rule.
